findings.locator: Results: Subject participation; Figure2; STAR Methods psychological measures and Participants
findings.population: Adults able to follow English instructions, mostly Stanford psychology recruits; exclusions for specified health/safety conditions
findings.design: Randomized four-arm active-comparator trial; this finding is an uncontrolled WITHIN-ARM pre/post contrast, not the randomized contrast
findings.sample: 108 participants overall; not all daily observations complete
findings.exposure: Five-minute daily cyclic-sighing practice with two-stage inhalation and prolonged exhalation
findings.comparator: The same person's before-session report; NO untreated counterfactual in this contrast
findings.measurement: STAI-state current-feeling score, separate from PANAS and trait anxiety
findings.result: State-anxiety reports fell after sessions in all four arms. This does not establish a specific cyclic-sighing advantage.
findings.limitations: Unblinded exploratory study, retrospective registration, selected sample, adherence missingness and no untreated arm; no enduring trait/clinical generalization.

findings.locator: Results: Breathwork...positive affect; Figure2D between-group mixed model
findings.design: Randomized active comparator; combined breathwork groups not cyclic-sighing-specific estimate
findings.sample: Same108 overall; repeated observations not independent samples
findings.result: No significant between-group difference in state-anxiety change; positive-affect superiority is a different outcome.
findings.limitations: Nondetection not equivalence. Combined operations cannot identify one technique's effect; no transfer from positive-affect advantage.

findings.locator: Results subject participation; FigureS4 described in main text
findings.design: Same randomized study; trait measure reported as separate outcome
findings.sample: Same108 overall, endpoint-specific complete N not extracted
findings.result: No detected trait-anxiety changes or between-group differences.
findings.limitations: OUTSIDE the proposed state endpoint; retained to prevent state-to-trait overclaim, not evidence that state effect equals zero.

findings.locator: Methods pp1156–1158; Results3 pp1160–1161; discussion p1168
findings.context: Individual screens/headphones in partitioned small laboratory groups
findings.design: Pseudo-random assignment to seven groups, counterbalanced film sets/order; repeated-measures stimulus validation, not fully randomized efficacy trial
findings.sample: 364; each viewed10clips from70, including neutral and multiple emotion categories
findings.exposure: Specified film excerpts selected for emotional content; standardized preparation across conditions
findings.comparator: Other film categories and within-category comparisons of target versus nontarget emotional ratings
findings.measurement: French modified DES sad/downhearted/blue1–7; retrospective feeling during the clip
findings.timing: Rating immediately after each clip following common relaxation preparation
findings.result: Film category altered emotional profiles; selected target emotions differentiated. Extracted target-versus-other-emotion tests are NOT the same-item sadness-versus-neutral effect required by the candidate.
findings.limitations: Mixed feelings, demand/selection and exact clip/content/language limits. Anger versus fear failed differentiation at category level. No universal sadness or persistent mood inference.

findings.population: Internet research samples from included studies; detailed demographics not extracted
findings.exposure: Various online affect-induction methods including video
findings.measurement: General affect and distinct emotion outcomes, including sadness
findings.timing: Study-specific short-term assessments not fully extracted
findings.result: Review reports effective sadness and several other discrete-emotion inductions; happiness induction was not significant.
findings.limitations: Background support for plausibility, not exact operation/clip/comparator. Happiness nondetection is not sadness null; inclusion overlap with other reviews unresolved.

findings.timing: Not an exact clip-specific time estimand
findings.result: Average induction effectiveness varies by method, target emotion and sample; broad pooled evidence does not identify every discrete Driver effect.
findings.limitations: Review components may overlap FilmStim/earlier syntheses; no independent replication count, pooled weight or universal transfer.

happeningTypes.name: Perform a specified cyclic-sighing breathing sequence
happeningTypes.description: Deliberate performance of a specified repeated two-stage inhalation/prolonged-exhalation sequence. Identity only: not generic slow/coherent/box breathing, not a clinical prescription, efficacy claim or practitioner permission.
happeningTypes.actor: Consenting participant in a supervised/approved research protocol
happeningTypes.constraints: Independent medical/safety/ethical screening, feasibility and actor control not assessed here; study excluded multiple conditions. Identity does not imply safety for an individual or benefit.

happeningTypes.name: Present a specified audiovisual film excerpt for attentive viewing
happeningTypes.description: Deliberate presentation of a specified audiovisual excerpt with viewing instructions. Clip/language/version identified in each scoped effect; identity does not promise an emotional response, scientific fidelity, diagnosis, or practitioner permission.
happeningTypes.actor: Research presenter controlling the specified licensed material
happeningTypes.constraints: Consent, distress/withdrawal and aftercare safeguards, copyright/license and cultural/language fit independently required. No film assets downloaded or published; not the earlier repeated-claim/refutation or Cyberball identity.

assertions.scope: Question: does specified cyclic sighing change current anxiety intensity beyond a matched attention/control condition in comparable screened adults? No universal decrease or clinical/trait benefit is asserted.
assertions.risk: Pre/post improvement alone does not identify efficacy; pooled breathwork is not a single technique. Expectancy, adherence, comparator and STAI construct overlap limit inference. No personal medical recommendation.
assertions.timing: Immediately before/after specified brief sessions; four-week repeated design, not lasting trait change
assertions.measurement: STAI-state current feelings; not STAI-trait, PANAS positive affect, respiration or physiological arousal
assertions.mechanism: Breathing/attention may influence subjective state, but no independently identified mediator or respiration-to-anxiety numerical propagation.
assertions.rationale: Source findings preserve uncontrolled within-arm improvement, active-comparator nondetection and separate trait null. They do not establish a signed technique-specific causal effect; exact follow-up needed.

assertions.scope: Question: can specified sadness-eliciting clips change current sadness relative to specified neutral clips in comparable French-speaking young adult viewers? Exact clip list and same-item contrast remain unresolved; no universal film effect.
assertions.risk: Target-versus-nontarget emotion differences within a clip category do not equal same-item sadness-versus-neutral contrasts. Mixed emotions, language, demand and sample composition limit inference. No mood/depression/comprehension effect.
assertions.timing: Reported immediately after clip about feelings DURING that clip; no persistence claim
assertions.measurement: Modified DES sad/downhearted/blue item-group1–7; NOT PANAS negative affect, K6 depression, general emotional-intensity arousal or all-negative-emotion composite
assertions.mechanism: Content/appraisal route plausible, but no mediator isolated. Film-world event is not an actual loss or a PSYWERX Relationship.
assertions.rationale: Primary stimulus validation and reviews support plausibility, but extracted contrasts do not establish the exact requested comparator and scope. Leave direction UNKNOWN rather than promote a broad common-knowledge effect.
